summary.text: Israel's new parliament, the 26th Knesset, is sworn in on Tuesday 10 November. Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival, has the first chance to form a government, and his opposition bloc announced an initial deal on appointments, including nominating Matan Kahana for Knesset speaker.

conclusion.text: All sides report the Knesset swearing-in and Eisenkot's bid to form a government. Western outlets frame it around ousting Netanyahu, while Eastern outlets lead with the opposition's appointments deal and a planned right-wing protest. Western outlets differ on whether Eisenkot's camp holds a majority.
